questions.question: Can transient Fzd signaling separate AT2 expansion from later alveolar maturation?
hypotheses: H1 temporal separation of expansion and maturation with retained reserve
H2 initial-state competence modifies the schedule response
H3 receptor-level input tunes activity trajectory and later fate balance
questions.unit: independent animal/donor/preparation; repeated wells and cells nested
questions.primary_outcome: mature lineage-descendant yield per initial viable labeled population
required_evidence: retained AT2 capacity and subsequent response
questions.biological_hypothesis: Fzd signaling maintains an expandable AT2 state; verified termination permits competent descendants to mature while preserving a responsive AT2 reserve.
questions.biological_process: reversible transition from expansion to mature alveolar contribution
questions.mechanistic_prediction: Linked descendants increase mature output after verified off-period without exhausting the retained AT2 reserve.

questions.question: Do subtype-specific Fzd signals maintain a fibroblast niche that enables alveolar maturation?
hypotheses: H1 greater loss of AF1 trophic activity and epithelial mature output after Fzd2 loss than Fzd1 loss
H2 relative receptor dependence differs by initial fibroblast subtype
questions.unit: independent fibroblast source/animal/preparation with epithelial recipient identity
questions.primary_outcome: absolute mature epithelial output; matrix remodeling assessed separately
questions.biological_hypothesis: Fzd2 maintains AF1-like trophic activity that enables AT2 descendant maturation; Fzd1-rich contexts are not automatically interchangeable support states.
questions.biological_process: receptor-dependent control of a functional fibroblast support state
questions.mechanistic_prediction: Comparable receptor loss alters functional fibroblast-derived support and subsequent epithelial maturation; source/recipient separation and restoration distinguish trophic activity from depletion.

questions.question: Does Fzd4 signaling recruit general-capillary cells into regenerative renewal after injury?
hypotheses: Fzd4-dependent regenerative state entry and later lineage contribution
questions.unit: independent animal/preparation with resolved round and capillary context
questions.primary_outcome: traced capillary descendant yield per initial viable labeled population
questions.biological_hypothesis: Fzd4 contributes to injury-induced gCap recruitment into a regenerative state that supplies renewed gCap and aerocyte descendants.
questions.mechanistic_prediction: Verified perturbation changes regenerative-state entry before traced descendant production, with an effect distinguishable from generalized endothelial loss.

deferred.Nb2-N8: Ligand-selective perturbation crossed with Fzd6 dependency absent

framing_rule: Each RQ states a plausible biological process, a causal/directional prediction, competing explanations and a discriminating outcome. Measurement artifacts motivate controls, not standalone biological hypotheses.
